mainEntity.name: What is the cost of an unfilled position?

acceptedAnswer.text: Cost of vacancy estimates the financial impact of leaving a role open — daily lost output or service capacity, overtime, temporary staff, and delayed projects. The EarlyJobs calculator multiplies vacancy days by your daily impact estimate and adds coverage costs you enter.

mainEntity.name: Is vacancy cost the same as cost per hire?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Vacancy cost is about money lost while the seat is empty; cost per hire measures recruitment spending to fill it. Leaders need both: high vacancy cost justifies faster hiring spend, while cost per hire shows whether sourcing is efficient.

mainEntity.name: Can the calculator be used for manufacturing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Plant and operations teams can model unfilled operator, maintenance, or QC roles using line-specific daily impact and shift overtime. Use conservative assumptions you can explain to plant heads rather than industry averages you cannot verify.

mainEntity.name: Does the calculator predict exact losses?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. It produces estimates from your inputs for planning and prioritisation, not statutory reporting. Revisit assumptions when production targets, customer SLAs, or staffing models change.

mainEntity.name: Is the Vacancy Cost Calculator free?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. This vacancy cost tool is free on EarlyJobs. Pair it with the Recruiting ROI or recruitment funnel calculators when building a case to shorten time-to-fill for critical roles.
